what_changed_my_mind: My first pass judged the hi tail in isolation - «3 अन्य लोग» is correct Hindi on its own, so I recorded the value as clean. It is not read in isolation: src/renderer/src/features/team-bridge/team-bridge-member-events.tsx:96-104 splices the rendered tail as the LAST element of the {targets} list, and five of the eleven hi event lines put {targets} immediately before a postposition (invited/removed/consented «को», declined/withdrawn «के लिए»). Hindi requires the oblique form before a postposition, so the spliced noun must be «लोगों», not «लोग».

added_findings.current: {count, plural, one {# अन्य व्यक्ति} other {# अन्य लोग}}
added_findings.proposed: revert to {count, plural, one {# अन्य} other {# अन्य}}
added_findings.reason: The invariant bare «अन्य» is the only tail that survives every position the list is spliced into; any head noun the tail gains must agree in case with a postposition it cannot see. Adding «व्यक्ति/लोग» therefore fixes the isolated string and breaks five call sites: the direct forms render «… और 3 अन्य लोग को आमंत्रित किया» and «… 3 अन्य लोग के लिए आमंत्रण अस्वीकार कर दिया», where Hindi needs «लोगों». Reverting restores «… 3 अन्य को आमंत्रित किया» / «… 3 अन्य के लिए …», which is grammatical because अन्य does not inflect.
added_findings.evidence: compose-hi.txt beside this record: the tail rendered through the repo's intl-messageformat and re-embedded in the actual sentence values at all seven hi positions, with the round-1 tail through the same positions for comparison.
added_findings.disposition: fix recommended (revert the tail, or restructure so the tail is never spliced into a case-governed position - a larger change than this delta)
